records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ μέγα καὶ θαυμαστόν, ἀγγέλους ἑπτὰ ἔχοντας πληγὰς ἑπτὰ τὰς ἐσχάτας, ὅτι ἐν αὐταῖς ἐτελέσθη ὁ θυμὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: And I saw another sign in the heaven great and wonderful, angels seven having plagues seven the last, because in them was completed the wrath of the God.
pieces: Then I saw another sign in heaven, great and astonishing: seven angels with seven plagues, the last plagues, for with them God's wrath is brought to an end.

L.1: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and wonderful: seven angels having seven plagues, the last ones, because in them the wrath of God is completed.

R.1: Then I saw another great and amazing sign in heaven. There were seven angels with seven plagues. These are the last plagues, because they finish God's anger.

decisions.choice: the last plagues: God's wrath brought to completion
decisions.reason: After the seals and trumpets, the bowls (chapter 16) are the last series of judgments. ἐτελέσθη is a past tense used of what is sure: with them God's wrath reaches its end. The three signs of the book are the woman (12:1), the dragon (12:3), and now these angels.

decisions.choice: sign
decisions.reason: Sign is a key term, kept at every level.

records.heading: Seven angels with the last plagues

records.source: Καὶ εἶδον ὡς θάλασσαν ὑαλίνην μεμιγμένην πυρί, καὶ τοὺς νικῶντας ἐκ τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ἐκ τῆς εἰκόνος αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκ τοῦ ἀριθμοῦ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν τὴν ὑαλίνην, ἔχοντας κιθάρας τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: And I saw as a sea glassy having been mixed with fire, and those overcoming out of the beast and out of the image of it and out of the number of the name of it standing on the sea the glassy, having harps of the God.
pieces: I saw something like a sea of glass with fire mingled in it. By the glassy sea stood those who had overcome the beast, its image, and the number of its name, and they held harps of God.

L.2: And I saw [something] like a sea of glass mixed with fire, and those who had overcome the beast and its image and the number of its name, standing by the sea of glass, holding harps of God.

R.2: I saw something that looked like a sea of glass mixed with fire. Standing beside it were the people who had won the victory over the beast, its statue, and the number of its name. God had given them harps to hold.

decisions.choice: a sea of glass mixed with fire, and the victors beside it: the crossing of the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The sea of glass is the one before the throne (4:6), now mixed with fire, the fire of judgment. The victors stand beside it and sing the song of Moses (15:3), as Israel stood on the shore of the Red Sea and sang after God brought them through and judged their enemies (Exodus 14-15).

decisions.choice: those who overcame: they came out victorious over the beast
decisions.reason: νικῶντας with ἐκ, "out of", is unusual: they have overcome and come out free from the beast, its image and its number (13:14-18). Their victory was faithfulness, even to death (12:11).

decisions.choice: on or beside the sea
decisions.reason: ἐπὶ with this case can mean "on" or "by". Like Israel at the Red Sea, they most likely stand on its shore.

decisions.choice: harps of God: given by God, for his praise
decisions.reason: The genitive can mean harps that belong to God's worship or harps God has given (compare 5:8; 14:2).

records.source: καὶ ᾄδουσιν τὴν ᾠδὴν Μωϋσέως τοῦ δούλου τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τὴν ᾠδὴν τοῦ ἀρνίου λέγοντες· Μεγάλα καὶ θαυμαστὰ τὰ ἔργα σου, κύριε, ὁ θεός, ὁ παντοκράτωρ· δίκαιαι καὶ ἀληθιναὶ αἱ ὁδοί σου, ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν αἰώνων·
records.gloss: And they sing the song of Moses the slave of the God and the song of the Lamb, saying: Great and wonderful the works of you, Lord the God the Almighty; righteous and true the ways of you, the King of the ages.
pieces: They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb: "How great and wonderful are {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works, Lord God, the Almighty! Your ways are just and true, King of the ages!

L.3: And they sing the song of Moses the slave of God and the song of the Lamb, saying, "Great and wonderful [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works, Lord God the Almighty; righteous and true [are] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways, King of the ages.

R.3: They sing the song of Moses, God's servant, and the song of the Lamb: "Lord God, the Almighty, the things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do are great and wonderful! King forever, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} ways are right and true!

decisions.choice: the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb: a new exodus
decisions.reason: Moses and Israel sang after crossing the Red Sea (Exodus 15), and Moses taught Israel a song of God's faithfulness (Deuteronomy 32). The song of the Lamb is the same song: the Lamb's victory is the greater exodus, and it is sung by those he has set free. Moses is called God's slave as in Numbers 12:7 and Joshua 1:2.

decisions.choice: great and wonderful works, just and true ways: the psalms and Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The words are drawn from the Old Testament: "Great are the works of the LORD" (Psalm 111:2), "wonderful are your works" (Psalm 139:14), "all his ways are justice ... just and upright is he" (Deuteronomy 32:4).

decisions.choice: King of the ages
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads αἰώνων, "of the ages". Other manuscripts read "of the nations", which fits Jeremiah 10:7 and the next verse; later ones read "of the saints". The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: King of the ages (L, B); King forever (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "of the ages" means.

decisions.choice: your: deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The song is sung to God.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it (1:1); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: τίς οὐ μὴ φοβηθῇ, κύριε, καὶ δοξάσει τὸ ὄνομά σου, ὅτι μόνος ὅσιος;
records.gloss: Who not not will fear, Lord, and will glorify the name of you? because alone holy;
pieces: Lord, who will not fear and glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name? Only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are holy.

L.4: Who will not fear [{{deity_pronoun:you|You}}], Lord, and glorify {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name? For {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone [are] holy.

R.4: Lord, everyone will fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and give glory to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, because only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are holy.

decisions.choice: Who will not fear you? Jeremiah 10:7
decisions.reason: "Who would not fear you, O King of the nations?" (Jeremiah 10:7). The question expects the answer: no one. Everyone will fear and honor God.

decisions.choice: alone holy
decisions.reason: ὅσιος means holy in the sense of pure and faithful. Only God is wholly so; no beast or ruler may claim it.

decisions.choice: a statement (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into what it means: everyone will fear God (m1).

records.source: ὅτι πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἥξουσιν καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν ἐνώπιόν σου, ὅτι τὰ δικαιώματά σου ἐφανερώθησαν.
records.gloss: because all the nations will come and will worship before you, because the righteous acts of you were revealed.
pieces: Every nation will come and worship in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence, because {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} acts of justice are now plain for all to see."

L.4: For all the nations will come and worship before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteous acts have been revealed."

R.4: All the nations will come and worship {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, because everyone has seen the right things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done."

decisions.choice: all the nations will come and worship: Psalm 86:9
decisions.reason: "All the nations you have made shall come and worship before you, O Lord, and shall glorify your name" (Psalm 86:9). The hope of the nations' worship runs through the book (5:9; 7:9; 21:24-26).

decisions.choice: your righteous acts: God's just deeds, including his judgments
decisions.reason: δικαιώματά can mean righteous deeds or just decrees. Here it is God's acts of justice, now made plain for all to see.

records.source: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἠνοίγη ὁ ναὸς τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ ἑπτὰ ἄγγελοι οἱ ἔχοντες τὰς ἑπτὰ πληγὰς ἐκ τοῦ ναοῦ, ἐνδεδυμένοι λίνον καθαρὸν λαμπρὸν καὶ περιεζωσμένοι περὶ τὰ στήθη ζώνας χρυσᾶς.
records.gloss: And after these things I saw, and was opened the temple of the tent of the testimony in the heaven, \v 6 and came out the seven angels the [ones] having the seven plagues out of the temple, having been clothed in linen pure bright and having been girded around the chests with sashes golden.
pieces: Then I looked, and in heaven the temple, the tent of witness, stood open.
From the temple the seven angels who held the seven plagues came out, robed in pure linen that shone, with gold sashes bound around their chests.

L.5: And after these things I looked, and the temple of the tent of witness in heaven was opened,
L.6: and the seven angels who had the seven plagues came out of the temple, clothed in pure, bright linen and with golden sashes wrapped around their chests.

R.5: After this I looked, and I saw that the temple in heaven was open. It was the tent where God's covenant was kept.
R.6: The seven angels with the seven plagues came out of the temple. They wore clean, shining linen clothes and gold sashes around their chests.

decisions.choice: the tent of witness: the tabernacle that held the covenant
decisions.reason: In the wilderness the tabernacle was called "the tent of witness" because it held the tablets of the covenant, the testimony (Exodus 38:21; Numbers 9:15; 17:7; Acts 7:44). The judgments come from the place of God's covenant: they are his faithfulness to it.

decisions.choice: linen
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads λίνον, "linen". Some important manuscripts read a word that differs by one letter and means "stone" (compare Ezekiel 28:13). The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: linen and gold sashes: the dress of priests
decisions.reason: Priests wore linen (Leviticus 16:4), and the risen Christ wears a golden sash (1:13). The angels come out of the temple as priests serving God.

decisions.choice: the tent where God's covenant was kept (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the tent of witness" (m1).

records.source: καὶ ἓν ἐκ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων ἔδωκεν τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλοις ἑπτὰ φιάλας χρυσᾶς γεμούσας τοῦ θυμοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων.
records.gloss: And one of the four living creatures gave to the seven angels seven bowls golden being full of the fury of the God the [one] living into the ages of the ages.
pieces: One of the four living creatures handed the seven angels seven gold bowls, full to the brim with the fury of the God who lives forever and ever.

L.7: And one of the four living creatures gave the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the fury of God, who lives for the ages of the ages.

R.7: One of the four living creatures gave each of the seven angels a gold bowl. The bowls were full of the anger of God, who lives forever and ever.

decisions.choice: golden bowls: the bowls of worship, now filled with wrath
decisions.reason: φιάλας are wide, shallow bowls used in temple worship. In 5:8 golden bowls held the prayers of the saints; now golden bowls hold God's wrath. The prayers are being answered.

records.source: καὶ ἐγεμίσθη ὁ ναὸς καπνοῦ ἐκ τῆς δόξης τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐκ τῆς δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὸν ναὸν ἄχρι τελεσθῶσιν αἱ ἑπτὰ πληγαὶ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων.
records.gloss: And was filled the temple with smoke from the glory of the God and from the power of him, and no one was able to enter into the temple until were completed the seven plagues of the seven angels.
pieces: Smoke from God's glory and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power filled the temple, and no one was able to enter it until the seven angels' seven plagues were finished.

L.8: And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power, and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.

R.8: The temple was filled with smoke, because God's glory and power were there. No one could go into the temple until the seven angels had finished pouring out the seven plagues.

decisions.choice: smoke filling the temple: God's glory at the tabernacle and temple
decisions.reason: When the tabernacle was finished, the glory of the LORD filled it and Moses could not enter (Exodus 40:34-35); at Solomon's temple the priests could not stand to minister (1 Kings 8:10-11); Isaiah saw the house filled with smoke (Isaiah 6:4). No one can enter or intercede until the judgments are done.
